about: The gate ladder: every leg of the gate of record that is not yet a Gradle task of its own. build-logic/src/main/kotlin/splice.gate-ladder.gradle.kts registers one Exec task per row under `gateOfRecord` (entered through `bun tools/gate run`), and tools/gate/test/run.test.ts reads the same rows WITHOUT Gradle to prove each one is a real leg: a unique task, a reason, and an argv whose target exists — it caught two legs still pointing into checks/ on 2026-09-21, after the move. The concentration leg's own routing check retired with the checker it routed; configguard.ts:11-13 records why. Each row declares `inputs`, the path globs its leg reads: pre-push scopes a push by them (tools/gate/src/lib/prepush-scope.ts), and run.test.ts fails a row that declares none. A row is data, not code: it is present or absent, and its argv is an array Gradle hands to the process without a shell. `why` is the leg's reason for existing — keep it when you move the leg.

legs.why: The ast-grep walls, then RULE ROUTING (the walls prove the routed rules pass and cannot prove they are ALL routed; .rules/kotlin sat unreferenced for a month reporting zero findings), then the CONFIG GUARD (no detekt baseline, maxIssues 0, every rule document severity:error, the dependabot scope, the concentration leg's routing), then the P1 coverage proof.
The Claude Code hook's red-green arms: the write-time wall (tools/gate/test/hook.test.ts).

Eleven frozen request/response scenarios grade the built Kotlin gateway byte-for-byte against the captured Node oracle. Keeping the replay as a package script without a gate leg left the parity claim entirely opt-in. It depends on :app:shadowJar because it judges the fat jar: without the dependency it ran first, found no jar and BUILT one through a nested gradle inside the gate (measured 2026-09-21).

Every message class a Claude Code session depends on (background-subagent task notifications, SessionStart hook context, cross-session messages, the date and <total_tokens> notices, free-form MCP tool schemas, reasoning blocks) through every dialect x system_prompt_mode of the built fat jar against a loopback fake upstream, one asserted cell each plus the system seam of each dialect x mode, and a census whose dialects and modes are read from the Kotlin source. V4-277 (a replace-mode chat head dropped every mid-conversation role=system message, so a subagent's result never reached the model) passed every unit test and only a request through the whole head could have caught it. No network, no quota; it judges the fat jar, so it depends on :app:shadowJar for the reason oracleReplay does.

The real launch shim records the PID and exact process birth that survive exec, including wrapped Claude and flag-first administrative logins. A missing-writer mutant fails, and an unrelated JVM cannot declare another parent. Loopback fixtures only, no provider login; the packaged CLI requires the freshly built jar.
94 strict TypeScript errors accumulated in tools/e2e because its older per-file debt baseline masked the project. Check the whole project without a baseline so new drift fails CI immediately.

Exercises the fat JAR the build produced, with synthetic auth and loopback-only tools. The receipt goes under app/build/ — never the tree. The leg owns its receipt and removes it when it starts, so a rerun writes its own; the mock still refuses any receipt that is there and was not removed by this leg.

bun audit --audit-level=critical over bun.lock, three attempts capped at a minute each (checks/oss/verify-OSS-I.sh until PR 6): the registry's advisory endpoint has hung and answered 503 mid-gate, and a critical advisory must still red all three attempts.

Operator rule 2026-09-18: this repo has no Python — tooling is bun/TypeScript. The rule drifted every time it was only prose, because nothing failed when a session added another .py. It is a wall now; the dated burn-down list beside this table is the debt and may only shrink. The PreToolUse guard (.claude/settings.json) is `bun tools/gate no-python --guard`, the same library rather than a reimplementation.

Nothing in the gate ran tsc: bun executes TypeScript without checking it, so a campaign wall carried 19 errors the gate's own tsconfig reported and no leg read, and 49 of 437 tracked .ts files sat in no program (2026-09-23). Every tracked .ts is now in a program or excused by name, and tools/gate/config/typecheck.json's per-file baseline is the older debt, which may only shrink.

Every red-green arm of the gate CLI: the slot, the JDK resolver, the title preflight, rule routing, the config guard, the no-python wall (every census RED on its mutation, and the write guard still refusing a synthetic event), the write-time hook and the coverage proof.

The release tooling's own red-green arms, which shipped with no row and so ran in nothing: dist's disposition law (an undispositioned file, a directory and a blank reason each fail BY NAME, with a placeholder-word positive control so the reason check is not vacuous), accept's semantic floor (a zero-byte artifact is EMPTY rather than present, a checksum that is not the file's own fails, the launcher and the jar must agree on a version, and an unmutated bundle passes every leg and still reds on the SBOM), the launch shim's arms measured against the SHIPPED shim (no fake curl survives — it speaks node:http, so PATH mocks are java and systemctl only), promote's abort paths (mismatched confirmation, EOF, main moving under the prompt, an existing tag, a missing or failing gh, each named rather than a silent exit 1), release.yml's legs (the gated stage command spelled exactly once, a comment decoy that passes a text check and fails this one, the asset list checked in both directions), verify's verb surface and zip's STORED/DEFLATED reads. Hermetic: every fixture is an mkdtemp under the OS temp dir, so the row needs no slot and no jar.
The commit subject against the conventional-type vocabulary; in CI the org gate judges the PR title instead.

splice is public: no commit HEAD reaches carries a Claude-Session trailer, a claude.ai session URL, a Co-Authored-By for noreply@anthropic.com or a Generated-with-Claude-Code line. The whole history is scanned, not the PR's commits, because a branch cut from the pre-rewrite tip carries the old attributed commits back in; a shallow CI clone is deepened blobless first and an unreadable history fails.
Two layers, deliberately. The generator makes the hazards inexpressible (#924); the canary selftest is defence in depth over its OUTPUT, so a bug in the generator itself still gets caught.
